### Fixed
- **The hook Jobs are policed by the chart** (giantswarm/agent-platform#413): every hook of this chart — the kagent namespace hook, the two storage-version hooks, the self hooks, the ordered teardown — runs `kubectl` against the apiserver under the hook identity's pod labels (`app.kubernetes.io/instance: <release>`, `app.kubernetes.io/component: hooks`), and the chart rendered no network policy for them; on a cluster that is default-deny for every endpoint (Cilium `policyEnforcementMode: always`) the `pre-upgrade` backup hook of 4.7.13+ looped on `dial tcp <apiserver>:443: i/o timeout` until its deadline and every meta-chart upgrade failed — the first 4.x installation sat on 4.7.12 from 2026-09-11 23:55Z for that reason. `templates/hooks/netpol.yaml` renders one policy for the hook identity **as a hook object** (a `pre-install`/`pre-upgrade` hook runs before the release's manifests exist): weight -10 next to the identity's ServiceAccount and ClusterRoleBinding, the same delete policy, at all five hook events with the bundled engine and at the storage-version hooks' four without it; egress to the apiserver only — the `kube-apiserver` entity in the cilium flavour, `networkPolicy.kubernetes.apiServerCIDR` in the kubernetes one — gated on `networkPolicy.enabled` and `networkPolicy.flavor` like every policy the platform renders. `make verify-hooks-netpol` asserts both flavours, the events per engine shape, the off switches and that every hook Job's pod carries the selected labels. An installation that hand-wrote such a policy (the connectivity hooks' sibling, #367) can drop the meta release's copy once this release is in. **No fleet installation acts** — the release stays inert behind the fleet's `<4.0.0` bound.
- **The storage-version backup hook no longer lists the cluster's Helm release Secrets with their payloads in one call** (giantswarm/agent-platform#414): the re-point step (#398) fetched every `helm.sh/release.v1` Secret cluster-wide through a client-side `jsonpath` listing — `kubectl get` collects the whole objects before such a printer runs — so the pod's memory grew with the cluster's Helm history and was OOM-killed at its 128Mi limit on the first 4.x installation (351 release Secrets, 61 MB of payload), failing the hook right after `no kagent CRD stores v1alpha2: nothing to migrate`. The listing is now the apiserver's Table (`kubectl get … --no-headers`, names only), each Secret is read and decoded on its own onto the emptyDir as before, and `jq` runs only on a manifest that names `kagent.dev/v1alpha2` at all (`grep` first) — memory bounded by the largest single release, not their sum. `make verify-kagent-storage-version` asserts the Table listing, the absence of a client-side printer and the pre-filter ahead of `jq`.
